akhfash:2-2.t: He said: ﴿أَنَّ لَهُمْ قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ﴾. "القدم" here means precedence (al-taqdīm), as you say: "هؤلاء أَهْلُ القَدَمِ في الأَسلام" (these are the people of precedence in Islam), i.e. those who sent forward good and so had precedence in it.

akhfash:5-5.t:
He said: ﴿وَقَدَّرَهُ مَنَازِلَ﴾, doubled; he made (وَقَدَّرُهُ) one of the verbs that take two objects, as though it were "وجعله منازل" (and He made it stations). And He said ﴿جَعَلَ ٱلشَّمْسَ ضِيَآءً وَٱلْقَمَرَ نُوراً﴾, making the moon itself the light, just as you say "جَعَلَهُ اللهُ خَلْقاً" (Allah made it a creation) when it is "created", and "هذا الدِرْهَمُ ضَرْبُ الأَمِير" (this dirham is the emir's minting) when it is "minted". And He said ﴿وَقُولُواْ لِلنَّاسِ حُسْناً﴾, making "الحسن" (goodness) the thing done, like "الخلق" (creation).
And He said ﴿وَقَدَّرَهُ مَنَازِلَ﴾ although He had mentioned the sun and the moon, just as He said ﴿وَٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ﴾.

akhfash:9-9.t: He said: ﴿يَهْدِيهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِإِيمَانِهِمْ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهِمُ ٱلأَنْهَارُ﴾. It is as though He made (تَجْرِي) a new beginning, cut off from what precedes.

akhfash:12-12.t:
He said: ﴿كَأَن لَّمْ يَدْعُنَآ إِلَىٰ ضُرٍّ مَّسَّهُ﴾ and ﴿كَأَن لَّمْ يَلْبَثُوۤاْ إِلاَّ سَاعَةً﴾. This is frequent in speech. It is the heavy "كَأَنَّ", but a pronoun is implied in it, so it is lightened, just as (أَنَّ)* is lightened with a pronoun implied in it; it is really "كَأَنْهُ لَمْ". The poet said [in the khafīf metre, and it is the two hundred and twenty-eighth poetic witness]:
*وَيْ كَأَنْ مَنْ يَكُنْ لَهُ نَشَبٌ يُحْبَبْ وَمَنْ يَفْتقِرْ يَعِشْ عَيْشُ ضرِّ*
(Ah, it seems that whoever has wealth is loved, and whoever becomes poor lives a life of hardship.)
And as he said [in the hazaj metre, and it is the two hundred and twenty-ninth poetic witness]:
[وصَدْرٍ مُشْرِقِ النَّحْرِ] * كَأَنْ ثَدْياهُ حُقّانِ
(And a bosom with a radiant throat, as though its breasts were two round caskets.)
i.e. "كَأَنْهُ ثَدْياهُ حُقَّانِ". Some recited "كَأَنْ ثَدْيْيهِ", lightening it and making it govern, without implying anything in it, as He said ﴿إِن كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمَا عَلَيْهَا حَافِظٌ﴾: he intended the meaning of the heavy form, so he made it govern as the heavy form governs, and did not imply a pronoun in it.

akhfash:19-19.t: He said: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ ٱلنَّاسُ إِلاَّ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾: as the khabar of "كان", just as He said ﴿إِن كَانَتْ إِلاَّ صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً﴾, [i.e.]* "it was nothing but a single cry".

akhfash:22-22.t:
He said: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا كُنتُمْ فِي ٱلْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم﴾. He said ﴿وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم﴾ only because (الفُلْكَ) may be singular or plural; He said ﴿فِي ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ﴾, where it is masculine. As for (حتَّى أَذا كُنْتُمْ في الفُلْكِ), its apodosis is His words ﴿جَآءَتْهَا رِيحٌ عَاصِفٌ﴾.
As for His words ﴿دَعَوُاْ ٱللَّهَ﴾, it is the apodosis of His words ﴿وَظَنُّوۤاْ أَنَّهُمْ أُحِيطَ بِهِمْ﴾. He said ﴿بِهِم﴾ although He had said ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ only because it is permissible to mention someone absent and then address him when you mean him, and to address and then put him in the wording of the absent, as in the poet's words [in the ṭawīl metre, and it is the one hundred and tenth poetic witness]:
أَسِيئِي بِنا أَوْ أَحْسِنِي لا مَلُوَمةً * لَدَيْنا وَلا مَقْلِيَّةً أَنْ تَقَلَّتِ
(Treat us ill or treat us well: you are not blamed by us, nor hated if she turns away in hatred.)

akhfash:23-23.t: He said: ﴿إِنَّمَا بَغْيُكُمْ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِكُمْ مَّتَاعَ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾, i.e. "and that is the enjoyment of the life of this world". He meant: "your enjoyment is the enjoyment of the life of this world".

akhfash:24-24.t:
He said: ﴿كَمَآءٍ أَنزَلْنَاهُ﴾, meaning "like the likeness of water".
And He said ﴿وَٱزَّيَّنَتْ﴾, meaning "وتَزَيَّنُتْ" (and it adorned itself), but the tāʾ was assimilated into the zāy because the two points of articulation are close; when its first letter became quiescent, a connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) was added to it. And He said ﴿وَٱزَّيَّنَتْ﴾, doubled — "ازَّيُّناً" if he means the maṣdar — and it is from "التَزَيْنِ" (adornment). He added the alif when he assimilated only so as to join the speech, since one cannot begin with a quiescent letter.

akhfash:26-26.t: He said: ﴿وَلاَ يَرْهَقُ وُجُوهَهُمْ قَتَرٌ وَلاَ ذِلَّةٌ﴾, because it is from "رَهَقَ" "يَرْهَقُ" "رَهَقاً". [Translator's note: the past tense is usually vocalised «رَهِقَ»; translated as written.]

akhfash:27-27.t:
He said: ﴿جَزَآءُ سَيِّئَةٍ بِمِثْلِهَا﴾: the bāʾ is added, just as it is added in your saying ﴿بِحَسْبِكَ قولُ السُوءِ﴾ (enough for you is evil speech). [Translator's note: this is an Arabic idiom, not a Qur'anic quotation, though the source places it in ﴿…﴾.]
And He said ﴿كَأَنَّمَا أُغْشِيَتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ قِطَعاً مِّنَ ٱلْلَّيْلِ مُظْلِماً﴾: the ṭāʾ is quiescent [Translator's note: the source says «العين», i.e. the ʿayn-position of the root, which is the ṭāʾ] because it is not the plural of "القِطْعَة" but "قِطْعٌ", a noun on its own. The generality of people read (قِطَعا), meaning by it the plural of "القِطْعَة". The first is supported by His words (مُظْلِماً), because "القِطْع" is singular, so "المُظْلِم" can be its adjective. Those who read "القِطَع", meaning the plural, said: "We make مُظلِماً a ḥāl of اللَيْل (the night)". The first is the clearer of the two ways.

akhfash:28-28.t: He said: ﴿مَكَانَكُمْ أَنتُمْ وَشُرَكَآؤُكُمْ﴾, because it has the meaning "انتْظِروا أنتم وشركاؤكم" (wait, you and your partners).

akhfash:30-30.t: He said: ﴿هُنَالِكَ تَبْلُواْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَّآ أَسْلَفَتْ﴾, i.e. it will experience. Some read (تَتْلُو), i.e. it will follow it.

akhfash:31-31.t:
He said: ﴿أَمَّن يَمْلِكُ ٱلسَّمْعَ وٱلأَبْصَارَ﴾. If you say: "How did (أَمْ) come before (مَنْ)?" — it is because (مَنْ) is not originally interrogative; it merely makes the alif unnecessary. That is why (أَمْ) was put before it, just as the interrogative particle was put before (هَلْ); the interrogative is originally only the alif. And (أَمْ) enters for a meaning that is indispensable. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre, and it is the two hundred and thirtieth poetic witness]:
أَبا مَالِكٍ هَلْ لُمْتَنِي مُذْ حَضَضْتِنَي * عَلَى القَتْلِ أَمْ هَلْ لامَنِي لَكَ لائِمُ
(Abū Mālik, have you blamed me since you urged me to the killing, or has any blamer blamed me on your account?)

akhfash:38-38.t: He said: ﴿فَأْتُواْ بِسُورَةٍ مِّثْلِهِ﴾. This is — and Allah knows best — "on the likeness of its sura", and he dropped "the sura", just as He said ﴿وَسْئَلِ ٱلْقَرْيَةَ﴾, meaning "the people of the town".

akhfash:50-50.t: He said: ﴿مَّاذَا يَسْتَعْجِلُ مِنْهُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾. If you wish, you may make (ماذا) a single noun with the status of (ما); and if you wish, you may make (ذا) have the status of "الذي" (which).

akhfash:53-53.t: He said: ﴿وَيَسْتَنْبِئُونَكَ أَحَقٌّ هُوَ﴾, as though He said "and they say: is it true?".

akhfash:58-58.t: He said: ﴿قُلْ بِفَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ وَبِرَحْمَتِهِ فَبِذَلِكَ فَلْيَفْرَحُواْ هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِّمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ﴾. Some read (تَجْمعَون), i.e. "what you amass, O company of unbelievers". Some read (فَلْتَفْرَحُوا); it is a poor dialect of the Arabs, because this lām enters only in a position where "أَفْعَل" (the direct imperative) cannot be used. They say "لِيَقُلْ زَيْدٌ" (let Zayd say) because you cannot use "أَفْعَل" [for an absent person]. The lām does not enter when you address a man: you say "قُلْ" (say) and do not need the lām. His words ﴿فَبِذَلِكَ﴾ are a badal (substitute) for His words ﴿قُلْ بِفَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ وَبِرَحْمَتِهِ﴾.

akhfash:61-61.t: He said: ﴿وَمَا يَعْزُبُ عَن رَّبِّكَ مِن مِّثْقَالِ ذَرَّةٍ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَلاَ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَلاَ أَصْغَرَ مِن ذٰلِكَ وَلاۤ أَكْبَرَ﴾, i.e. "and nothing smaller than that nor greater escapes Him", with the nominative. Some read (وَلا أصغرَ من ذلِكَ ولا أَكْبَرَ) with fatḥa, i.e. "nor of anything smaller than that nor of anything greater"; but it is "أَفْعَلَ" and is a diptote [so its genitive appears with fatḥa]. This is better in Arabic and more frequent in reading, and that is how we read.

akhfash:71-71.t:
He said: ﴿فَأَجْمِعُوۤاْ أَمْرَكُمْ وَشُرَكَآءَكُمْ﴾, and some read (وشُرَكاؤُكُمْ). The accusative is better, because you do not make an overt nominative noun follow a nominative pronoun [i.e. conjoin it to it]; but it has become acceptable here because of the separation between them, as He said ﴿أَإِذَا كُنَّا تُرَاباً وَآبَآؤُنَآ﴾, where it is good because He separated them by His word "تراباً". Some read (فَأَجْمِعوا), because they took it in the sense of "العَزْمِ" (resolve), since the Arabs say "أَجْمَعْتُ أَمْرِي", i.e. I resolved to say such-and-such, i.e. I determined upon it. And we read with the cut (hamzat al-qaṭʿ) alif. [Translator's note: the two forms (فَأَجْمِعُوا) are printed identically in the source; the variant is presumably «فَاجْمَعُوا» with a connecting alif.]
And He said ﴿ثُمَّ لاَ يَكُنْ أَمْرُكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ غُمَّةً﴾: (يَكُنْ) is jussive by the prohibition.

akhfash:77-77.t: He said: ﴿أَتقُولُونَ لِلْحَقِّ لَمَّا جَآءَكُمْ أَسِحْرٌ هَـٰذَا﴾: this is by way of quoting (ḥikāya) their words, because they said "Is this magic?", so He said (أَتَقَوُلُونَ) (أَسِحْرٌ هذا).

akhfash:78-78.t: He said: ﴿لِتَلْفِتَنَا﴾, because you say "لَفَتُهُ", so "أَنَا أَلِفْتُهُ" "لَفْتَاً", i.e. I turn him away from his due.

akhfash:81-81.t: He said: ﴿مَا جِئْتُمْ بِهِ ٱلسِّحْرُ﴾; he says: "That which you have brought is magic". Some read (آلسِّحْرُ) with the interrogative.

akhfash:83-83.t: He said: ﴿عَلَىٰ خَوْفٍ مِّن فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَئِهِمْ﴾, meaning the chiefs of the offspring (al-dhurriyya).

akhfash:88-88.t:
He said: ﴿رَبَّنَا ٱطْمِسْ عَلَىٰ أَمْوَالِهِمْ وَٱشْدُدْ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ فَلاَ يُؤْمِنُواْ﴾: he put it in the accusative because the answer to a supplication with fāʾ is accusative; likewise in supplication when they disobeyed.
And He said ﴿رَبَّنَا لِيُضِلُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِكَ﴾, i.e. "so they went astray", just as He said ﴿فَٱلْتَقَطَهُ آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوّاً وَحَزَناً﴾, i.e. "so he became". They did not pick him up in order that he become an enemy and a grief to them; [but] they picked him up and he became so. This lām comes in this meaning.
And His words ﴿فَلاَ يُؤْمِنُواْ﴾ are conjoined to (ليضلوّا).

akhfash:92-92.t:
He said: ﴿فَٱلْيَوْمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ﴾, and some read (نُنْجِيك). His words ﴿بِبَدَنِكَ﴾ mean: with no spirit in it.
Some said: (نُنُجِّيكَ) means "We shall raise you up on a height (najwa) of the land". Their saying that "البَدَن here is the coat of mail (الدِرْع)" is nothing and has no meaning.

akhfash:97-97.t: He said: ﴿وَلَوْ جَآءَتْهُمْ كُلُّ آيَةٍ﴾: He made the verb of "كلّ" feminine because He annexed it to "آية" (sign), which is feminine.

akhfash:99-99.t: He said: ﴿لآمَنَ مَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ كُلُّهُمْ جَمِيعاً﴾: He brought His words (جَمِيعاً) as tawkīd (emphasis), just as He said ﴿لاَ تَتَّخِذُواْ إِلـٰهَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ﴾, where in His word ﴿إِلـٰهَيْنِ﴾ there is already an indication of "two".

akhfash:103-103.t: He said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ حَقّاً عَلَيْنَا نُنجِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾; he says: "Thus do We save the believers — a duty upon Us".

akhfash:105-105.t: He said: ﴿وَأَنْ أَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفاً﴾, i.e. "and I have been commanded to set your face to the religion".
